rooms.title: La cocina de la abuela
rooms.subtitle: Grandma's kitchen
rooms.focus: Regular verbs: one clue per sentence

puzzles.sentence_pre: Todas las mañanas, en la radio
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Todas las mañanas" (every morning) marks a habit. Habits and repeated actions in the past take the imperfect: sonaban.
puzzles.translation: Every morning, old boleros used to play on the radio.

puzzles.sentence_pre: El viejo reloj de la pared siempre
puzzles.rule_feedback: This describes how the clock usually was, not one event. Descriptions and habits ("siempre") take the imperfect: marcaba.
puzzles.translation: The old wall clock was always five minutes slow.

puzzles.sentence_post: la cocina con una luz cálida.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Por las noches" (at night, every night) sets a repeated background scene. Use the imperfect: iluminaba.
puzzles.translation: At night, the lamp lit the kitchen with a warm light.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras la abuela cocinaba, la tetera
puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" (suddenly) marks a single action that interrupts the background ("cocinaba"). Sudden, completed actions take the preterite: empezó.
puzzles.translation: While grandma was cooking, the kettle suddenly started to whistle.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Entonces el gato saltó a la mesa y
puzzles.rule_feedback: This is a chain of completed events: first "saltó", then the next action. Events that move the story forward take the preterite: tiró.
puzzles.translation: Then the cat jumped onto the table and knocked a plate onto the floor.

rooms.title: El salón en invierno
rooms.subtitle: The living room in winter
rooms.focus: Common irregulars: hacer, poner, tener, venir, ser

puzzles.rule_feedback: Weather that sets the scene is background description, so it takes the imperfect: hacía. The preterite of hacer is irregular (hice, hizo), but it doesn't fit here.
puzzles.translation: It was winter and it was very cold outside.

puzzles.rule_feedback: Describing how people looked or what they were like takes the imperfect. Ser is irregular in the imperfect: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran.
puzzles.translation: In that photo, my grandparents were very young.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cada tarde" (every afternoon) is a routine, so use the imperfect: tenía. Tuvo (irregular stem tuv-) is for a single completed event.
puzzles.translation: Every afternoon, my sister had to practise the piano.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" signals one sudden, completed action, so use the preterite. Poner has an irregular stem, pus-: puse, pusiste, puso.
puzzles.translation: Suddenly, Dad put more wood in the fireplace.

puzzles.sentence_post: el tío Pepe con un regalo enorme.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Entonces" (then) moves the story forward with a new event, so use the preterite. Venir has an irregular stem, vin-: vine, viniste, vino.
puzzles.translation: Then Uncle Pepe came with an enormous present.

rooms.title: El dormitorio de la infancia
rooms.subtitle: The childhood bedroom
rooms.focus: Both tenses in one sentence, heavy irregulars: ser, ir, estar, caer

puzzles.sentence_post: pequeño, soñaba con viajar por todo el mundo.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cuando era pequeño" (when I was little) describes a stage of life, which is background. Use the imperfect: era. Careful: fui is the preterite of both ser and ir.
puzzles.translation: When I was little, I dreamed of travelling all over the world.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Cuando llegué a casa, el cielo
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Llegué" is the event; the sky is the scene it happened in. States and descriptions take the imperfect: estaba. Estuvo (stem estuv-) would mean a closed period.
puzzles.translation: When I got home, the sky was very cloudy.

puzzles.sentence_post: a la cama cuando, de repente, sonó el teléfono.
puzzles.rule_feedback: An action already in progress that gets interrupted ("sonó") takes the imperfect. Ir is one of only three irregular imperfects: iba, ibas, iba (the others are ser and ver).
puzzles.translation: I was already going to bed when, suddenly, the phone rang.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras yo dormía, un libro se
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Dormía" is the background; the book falling is the single event that interrupts it. Use the preterite. Caer changes i to y: cayó, cayeron.
puzzles.translation: While I was sleeping, a book fell off the shelf.

puzzles.sentence_post: al mercado y compré flores frescas.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Esa mañana" (that morning) points to one specific occasion, followed by another completed action ("compré"). Use the preterite: fui. It is the same form as ser's preterite, so context tells you which verb it is.
puzzles.translation: That morning I went to the market and bought fresh flowers.
